scenes.headline: Every app had [its own dashboard.]
scenes.punch: TCC puts every app on [one screen.]

vo.text: Tecstellar runs several consumer apps, and every one had its own dashboard. Users in one place, payments in another, and follow-ups nowhere at all.
The Command Center puts every app on one screen.

scenes.title: Tecstellar Command Center
scenes.tagline: One console for agents, supervisors and owners, across every app.

vo.text: It's one console in three roles. Agents work the phones, supervisors run the team, and owners see the whole portfolio.

scenes.headline: A calling desk that [never needs the mouse.]
bullets: Queues per app, follow-ups due today
1–5 for status, Q–I for outcome, Enter to save
A softphone that stays live across pages

vo.text: Agents start on today's queue, with follow-ups that are due and the numbers they're chasing.
The call panel runs on keyboard shortcuts, and the phone line stays live while they open a customer's history.

scenes.headline: See the team. [Fix the gaps.]
bullets: Calls, connect rate and sentiment by agent
Escalations land in a live inbox
Allocation shows states nobody can reach

vo.text: Supervisors see every agent's calls, connect rate and sentiment, take escalations from a live inbox, and spot the languages and states nobody on the team can reach.

scenes.headline: Every app's [users, revenue and funnel], together.
bullets: Customers, paying users and monthly revenue
Service health and a map of India

vo.text: Owners get one overview across every app: customers, revenue, dues, the funnel from sign-up to paying, and a D3 map of where users are.
It's a React and TypeScript app. With Firebase configured, calls, tickets and escalations sync live across every browser. Without it, the whole thing runs offline in local storage.
And because the sample customers have random phone numbers, calling has three safety modes: a test number, live, or locked.
Every app, every call, one console.
Read the full case study, and see how it was built.
